status: in progress; throughput and memory parity remain unmet
acceptance: Keep pursuing throughput and memory parity before accepting the pivot.
implementation: Pack the four-byte reliable record length and inline CBOR routing/control prefix into one small owned Bytes chunk, then submit that and a clone of the immutable payload using the direct WebTransport stream write_all_chunks API. QUIC retains the shared body for retransmission instead of allocating/copying a body per recipient. Framing, FIFO, routing, output reservation lifetime, per-record deadlines, crypto, congestion control and transport configuration are unchanged. Graceful close ACKs remain their original empty records.
tradeoffs: One owned header allocation plus a shared body reference per output record. This is not a zero-allocation or end-to-end zero-copy claim. Shared transport ownership can retain a backing allocation for longer; complete large-payload workloads are measured explicitly. 64 KiB RSS rises in this screen, while 1 MiB RSS falls substantially; neither workload shows a material throughput gain.
scope: Local Linux loopback; ordinary release builds and frozen verifying clients. Three alternating fresh-process repetitions per case/variant, no concurrent build/test/browser during timing. Four pinned server workers on CPUs 0-3, eight pinned client workers on CPUs 8-15, four seconds; main screen uses 1 KiB values, 32 private pairs, 1024 room readers, fanout window four. Large private screens use 64 KiB with 32 pairs and 1 MiB with four pairs. Capacity uses 100000 independently counted physical QUIC connections, eight server workers on CPUs 0-7, four offered seconds and 400000 exactly verified deliveries. Logarithmic latency percentiles are upper bounds. RSS is sampled at phase gates, excludes kernel socket memory and differs from continuous peak or requested live heap.

build.note: Final product files match timed candidate hashes; only a pressure fixture/test was added after timing. Rebuild byte equality checked against the measured executable.

heap-shared-session.scope: 8194 real sessions with replacement gperftools allocator; excluded from ordinary timing/RSS medians. Original three phase gates plus observations at 1/5 seconds while completed client held at done.

heap-direct-chunks.scope: 8194 real sessions with replacement gperftools allocator; excluded from ordinary timing/RSS medians. Original three phase gates plus observations at 1/5 seconds while completed client held at done.

profiles.scope: Privileged perf attachment only; relay/verifier run as normal user. User cycles sampled at 499 Hz with DWARF call graphs. Independent eight-second captures, excluded from ordinary medians. Self-sample percentages identify work, not a promised speedup or exact elapsed cost.
profiles.baseline_observation: Stream write_all self samples: 4.85% private, 4.30% mixed. Packet construction, buffer ownership and crypto also substantial. The earlier rejected chunk-write experiment at 9f82ba0 used the older transport driver and only 32-client private probes; new measurements use the current direct engine and full fanout/mixed verifiers.

validation.vendor: 152 files verified against four original archives and three declared patches; dependencies unchanged
validation.new_write_deadline: Real independent wtransport client: 64 KiB stream receive credit, unread 12 MiB private delivery exceeding the default 10 MB transport send window. Write timeout increments exactly once, queued/read budget credit releases, another room remains responsive before and after timeout, and shutdown clears connection/output metadata credit. Focused run plus full suite passed.
validation.browser: Chromium 155 actual delivered bundle, all nine checks passed: three sessions, typed broadcast, cross-room private, datagrams, 128 KiB/5 MiB values, concurrent variables, unsafe-number rejection, departure and genuine graceful closure. Seven final gauges zero.

historical_controls.scope: Previously measured controls, not rerun during this checkpoint. Plaintext remains the existing parity baseline. The encrypted fixture includes both proxy and backend CPU/RSS and an additional loopback hop; it is not a native-WSS performance ceiling.

freshness_scope: One candidate regression sample per clean/loss/reordering mode; 360 offered 1 KiB states at 60 Hz over six seconds with concurrent reliable 1 MiB bulk. Loss: 20 ms one-way and 2% packet loss; reordering adds 8 ms jitter and 25% reorder. Both directions, external port only, temporary isolated namespace, TLS fixture internal hop unimpaired. Matching seeds/parameters do not impose identical packet-loss trajectories. Probes include initial state before first update; stale sequences never replace fresh state. Missing means unreceived observations, not all attributed to network loss. No statistical protocol ranking is claimed.
remaining: Small-message throughput improves materially, but reliable room/mixed throughput and memory remain behind the earlier plaintext control. Mixed private traffic still trails the earlier encrypted fixture. Address large-record retained capacity and active QUIC/HTTP3 state, then reliable scheduling. Full observer cancellation/re-subscribe, concurrent 100k/8192 inspection, broader overload/shutdown/retirement fallback, QUIC buffer accounting and final packaging/deployment docs remain required. The new blocked-writer check covers one specific cancellation/deadline path. No acceptance or release claim.
